text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated egress packet loss observed from eu-west-1 -> AS65022 (provider-cedar). Loss spiking to ~12% for multiple /24s inside 3.120.0.0/16. Detected at 02:03 UTC. Severity: P2. Auto-runbook: /runbooks/network/egress-loss. Paging on-call.

maria.chen: I’m on it, grabbing context. Which AZs are affected?

sofia_ops: Looks like both eu-west-1a and 1b from our telemetry (agent-egress). Netflow shows retransmits upstream.

raj_kapoor: Confirmed from our edge mtr from euw1-edge-03: packetloss begins at provider hop 3. Local hops fine.

raj_kapoor: mtr summary:
```
Start: 2026-03-15 02:04:12
HOST: euw1-edge-03 Loss% Snt Last Avg Best Wrst StDev
1. 10.0.0.1 0.0% 100 0.2 0.4 0.1 8.0 0.8
2. 52.14.12.2 0.0% 100 1.2 1.8 1.1 23.3 2.1
3. 198.51.100.5 12.0% 100 14.2 16.9 13.1 89.0 9.6  <-- provider-cedar hop
4. 203.0.113.8 12.0% 100 15.3 17.1 14.5 92.4 10.1
```

maria.chen: Good catch. So this is upstream. Did we get any BGP updates/withdraws around the time?

net-bot: BGP flaps detected: AS65022 announced/withdrawn prefixes 3.120.0.0/16 (multiple /24s) 5 times in last 8 minutes. See logs: `bgp-logs/euw1/1975000000.log`

tom_sullivan: I’m going to open a ticket with provider-cedar NOC and share traceroutes. Also preparing traffic-shift play: move critical customers to backup provider (AS65077) via temporary prepend/localpref changes.

maria.chen: Before we shift, let's check if a community filter or AS-path prep is enough. Who owns the backup uplink at euw1-edge?

sofia_ops: Backup is via provider-pine (AS65077) and our link there has headroom. If we change export policy to prefer provider-pine for affected prefixes we can cut exposure.

raj_kapoor: Quick BGP show for affected prefix
```
show bgp ipv4 3.120.5.0/24 detail
BGP routing table entry for 3.120.5.0/24, version 12456
Paths: (2 available, best #1)
  Advertised to update-groups: 0
  65022 65010  -> via 198.51.100.5 (next hop) [euw1-edge-03]
    AS path: 65022 65010
  65077 65010  -> via 203.0.113.9 (next hop)
    AS path: 65077 65010
LocalPref: 100, Weight: 0
```

maria.chen: We can flip localpref to prefer 65077 for the impacted /24s only. That avoids global churn. Who will run?

tom_sullivan: I can push the change to the euw1 export policy. Will do a canary for two /24s first.

support-rotation: Heads up, support is seeing elevated 502/timeout errors for EU users hitting completions; incidence started ~02:05 UTC. Logging thread ID: INC-1975-euw1.

maria.chen: OK tag customers: app-prod-eu SaaS customers on those egress IPs see latency/errors. Support, please queue customer impact notifications for high-usage tenants. We’ll coordinate wording.

tom_sullivan: Pushing canary now. Config snippet I’ll apply (policy change):
```
policy-set export-euw1 {
  if prefix in ACL_IMPACTED then set local-pref 200 for neighbor 203.0.113.9;
}
```

tom_sullivan: Applied to euw1-edge-03 canary for prefixes 3.120.5.0/24 and 3.120.6.0/24. Monitoring BGP and path.

raj_kapoor: After localpref change, route switched to AS65077 for those two /24s. mtr shows immediate drop in loss to ~0.5% on those canary prefixes.

sofia_ops: Good. Can we scale to the rest of the /24s? Any risk of asymmetric return path for stateful flows?

maria.chen: Risk low — only changing egress preference, traffic still returns via provider selection. But open a check: persistent asymmetry could affect TCP handshake for some CDNs. We'll roll gradually.

tom_sullivan: Rolling to remaining impacted /24s now (staggered 30s). Will post progress.

net-bot: Change events recorded, RFC: CHG-1975-euw1-localpref.

maria.chen: Re: provider NOC — did we get a response?

tom_sullivan: Cedar NOC acknowledged at 02:12 UTC, investigating a fiber flap in their PoP. They report internal convergence causing dropped traffic for some transit paths. No ETA yet.

support-rotation: Support update: error rates for EU completions back down to baseline for canary tenants, but still elevated for others pending roll. Let me update customer-facing status page: "We are experiencing degraded connectivity to some EU regions; we are actively rerouting traffic to alternate providers."

sofia_ops: After full roll, overall packet loss to AS65022 decreased cluster-wide from 12% -> 1.2%. Edge telemetry shows normal latency.

raj_kapoor: Running longer MTRs to confirm stability, will leave for 15m.

maria.chen: Next steps: 1) Keep rollback runbook ready in case provider fix reverses. 2) Post-incident: request full MRT/BGP dump from provider-cedar for analysis. 3) Customer impact doc: estimate affected tenants and durations (support to draft). 4) Postmortem owner: raj_kapoor.

tom_sullivan: I'll keep the localpref policy in place until cedar confirms full fix. Will annotate change in config management.

incident-bot: NOTE: Incident severity downgraded to P3 at 02:18 UTC after mitigations. Continue monitoring.

maria.chen: Handing to raj for post-incident follow-up. Raj, do you want a handoff?

raj_kapoor: Taking postmortem. Will collect telemetry, BGP logs, and timeline. Support, please attach impacted customer list to INC-1975.

support-rotation: Will attach list and customer emails to the incident. Draft status update posted to status.redwood.ai/incident/1975 (internal).

sofia_ops: A note — we should add automated localpref failover to runbook for egress-loss to cut time to mitigation next time. Filing runbook FR.

maria.chen: Agreed. Thanks all. If anything regresses ping me. Closing coordination channel, leave thread open for postmortem artifacts.

raj_kapoor: Will post root cause timeline and mitigation details in this thread once done.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated by traffic reroute) at 02:23 UTC. Resolution comment: traffic shifted to provider-pine; provider-cedar investigating fiber/convergence issue.

maria.chen: Adding final note: no data loss, transient customer errors for ~18 minutes for some EU tenants. Postmortem ETA: 2026-03-17 18:00 UTC.

raj_kapoor: Copy. Closing out active on-call tasks, will follow up with a detailed postmortem.
